source_meta._title: Player-in-block checking happens after block collision events are done

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.12.2 in a new single-player Superflat world, using the integrated server. Use Survival mode with cheats enabled. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the currently bound Forward control instead of W if controls have been changed.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version Minecraft 1.12.2 with no mods, plugins, datapacks, or third-party server software.

Create a new single-player world through Singleplayer -> Create New World. Select Game Mode: Survival, then More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON and World Type: Superflat. No particular seed is required.
Use an expendable test world. The reproduction intentionally activates an End portal and may leave the player in a dangerous position after the dimension transition.
Keep the default Forward control bound to W, or identify the replacement key before beginning.
Do not use Creative flight, sprinting, sneaking, jumping, or strafing during the final movement step.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition 1.12.2, open the prepared Superflat test world, and wait without entering commands until the Overworld has finished loading.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld, nearby Superflat terrain is rendered, the HUD is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Create an elevated stone work platform so the setup has a deterministic Y coordinate and enough empty space around it. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /fill -4 79 -4 5 79 4 stone
steps.success_cue: A one-block-thick stone platform covering X=-4 through 5, Y=79, and Z=-4 through 4 is visible above the Superflat ground, and chat does not report a command error.

steps.action: Place the player at the deterministic reference position above the platform. Press T, enter the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on top of the elevated platform at approximately X=0.500, Y=80.000, Z=0.500.

steps.action: Place the End portal block specified by the report. While remaining at the reference position, press T, enter the report command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~2 ~ ~ end_portal
steps.success_cue: A horizontal, dark, star-like End portal surface is present at block coordinates X=2, Y=80, Z=0, two blocks in the positive-X direction from the reference block.

steps.action: Place the glass block specified by the report. Do not move from the reference position. Press T, enter the report command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /setblock ~1 ~ ~1 glass
steps.success_cue: A glass block is present at block coordinates X=1, Y=81, Z=0, immediately above the space between the player and the End portal block.

steps.action: Use the Minecraft 1.12.2-compatible teleport equivalent of the report's alignment command. The deterministic reference position makes floor-aligned X and Z equal to 0, so these absolute coordinates preserve the report's destination offsets and rotation. Press T, enter the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is positioned at approximately X=1.700, Y=80.000, Z=0.700005, facing diagonally toward the End portal, with the player's upper bounding box intersecting the adjacent glass block.

steps.action: Without pressing any movement key or moving the mouse, press F3 to open the debug screen and verify the forced position and rotation. Check for X near 1.700, Y near 80.000, Z near 0.700, horizontal rotation near -60 degrees, and vertical rotation near 0 degrees.
steps.exact_input: F3
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay confirms the approximate target coordinates and rotation; the player has not moved away from the forced glass intersection.

steps.action: Press F3 again to close the debug screen. Release all movement controls and do not rotate the camera after closing it.
steps.exact_input: F3
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is closed, the normal first-person view is visible, and the player remains facing the portal from the forced intersection position.

steps.action: Trigger the reproduction by pressing and holding the Forward control, W by default, without sprinting, jumping, sneaking, strafing, or turning the camera. Continue holding Forward until the End dimension-loading transition starts, then immediately release Forward. If no transition starts within five seconds, release Forward without making any other corrective movement.
steps.exact_input: W
steps.success_cue: Forward movement has been attempted from the forced glass-intersection position; if the portal activates, the dimension-loading screen begins.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just attempted forward movement from the forced glass-intersection position. If the End portal transition starts, release Forward and hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the End view begins rendering; do not move, teleport, respawn, or otherwise correct the player's position.
uncertainties: The report's literal command `/execute align xz run teleport @s ~1.7 ~ ~0.700005 -60 0` uses the rewritten command system and cannot be parsed by the selected first affected version, Minecraft 1.12.2. This plan therefore anchors the player at X=0.5, Y=80, Z=0.5 and uses the legacy-compatible equivalent `/tp @p 1.7 80 0.700005 -60 0`. Historical command documentation confirms that `/execute` was rewritten beginning in 17w45a and that the older `/tp` form accepts a target, coordinates, yaw, and pitch. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3A%E7%94%A8%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4%E6%93%8D%E6%8E%A7%E5%AE%9E%E4%BD%93?variant=zh-hk&utm_source=openai))

The report does not specify a game mode, world type, seed, or starting coordinates. Survival with cheats, a Superflat world, and an elevated platform at Y=79 are practical choices intended to provide deterministic empty space without changing the reported portal-and-glass geometry.

The command-based reproduction is treated as the primary procedure. Earlier comments describe more elaborate bed and glass setups and indicate that some manual variants may require multiple attempts, but those variants are not introduced because the report supplies a simpler precise command setup.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 19w14b in a single-player test world. Commands must be available, so create the world with Allow Cheats enabled or use another environment in which the executing player has command permission. Use a clear area with a solid, level floor and several blocks of unobstructed vertical space. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Launch the first affected version, Minecraft 19w14b; do not use fix version 24w37a for the reproduction.
Commands are enabled for the executing player.
The player is in a loaded area with a solid, level floor and enough overhead clearance to fly above a shulker.
No seed, coordinates, world type, dedicated server, or additional player is required by the report.
The deterministic closed-shulker variant from the report is used rather than the alternative Creative-player, invulnerable-mob, or breeze variants.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and launch the Java Edition installation for 19w14b. Do not continue until the main menu identifies the selected version as 19w14b.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft Java Edition 19w14b is running and its main menu is responsive.

steps.action: Create or load a disposable single-player world in which commands are enabled. If creating a world, enable Allow Cheats before entering it. Wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a responsive, fully loaded world and can execute commands.

steps.action: Move to a clear, level section of solid ground with several blocks of empty space above it. Stand still on the block where the shulker should be summoned; the supplied relative coordinates summon it at the player's current position.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on a solid floor in an unobstructed test area.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat control, whose default key is T.
steps.exact_input: T
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, spaces, capitalization, relative coordinates, braces, colon, and byte suffix. Press Enter once to execute it.
steps.exact_input: /summon shulker ~ ~ ~ {NoAI:1b}
steps.success_cue: A shulker has appeared at the player's location without a command syntax error.

steps.action: Move a short distance away from the summoned shulker so it is clearly visible. Confirm that it is attached to the floor and that its shell is closed. Do not attack it or place blocks that would force it to relocate.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: One stationary, closed shulker is visible on the floor in the clear test area.

steps.action: Open in-game chat again using the default chat key.
steps.exact_input: T
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: Set the executing player to Creative mode by entering the game-mode command, including the leading slash, and pressing Enter. This operationalizes the report's instruction to set the game mode to Creative.
steps.exact_input: /gamemode creative
steps.success_cue: The player is in Creative mode, with access to the Creative inventory and the ability to start flying by double-tapping Jump.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, whose default key is E.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface and its item-category tabs are visible.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon, and enter "bow" in its search field. Move one ordinary Bow from the search results into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.exact_input: bow
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Bow is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear the search field, enter "arrow", and move at least one ordinary Arrow into the player's inventory or hotbar. Use a normal Arrow rather than a tipped or spectral arrow.
steps.exact_input: arrow
steps.success_cue: The player possesses an ordinary Bow and at least one ordinary Arrow.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Escape. Select the hotbar slot containing the Bow using its number key or the mouse wheel. The selected slot is the active slot and is shown with a highlighted border.
steps.exact_input: E, then the Bow's hotbar number or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and the player is holding the Bow in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: Start Creative flight by pressing the Jump control twice in quick succession; the default Jump key is Space.
steps.exact_input: Space, Space
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended when no block is beneath their feet, confirming that Creative flight is active.

steps.action: While flying, hold Jump to ascend several blocks above the shulker. Use the movement controls to position the player directly over the center of the closed shulker rather than beside it. Stop moving once aligned.
steps.exact_input: Hold Space; use W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering above the shulker with a clear, unobstructed line to the top of its closed shell.

steps.action: Rotate the camera until it points straight downward and center the crosshair on the middle of the shulker's top face. The shot must be approximately vertical: do not aim at the side or fire from an oblique angle, because the report comments distinguish straight-down shots from angled shots that bounce away.
steps.exact_input: Mouse movement
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the top of the closed shulker while the player is hovering directly above it.

steps.action: Without changing position or aim, press and hold the Use Item control, whose default input is the right mouse button, until the Bow reaches its fully drawn visual state.
steps.exact_input: Hold right mouse button
steps.success_cue: The Bow is visibly fully drawn while the crosshair remains centered on the shulker's top face.

steps.action: Release the right mouse button to fire one arrow straight downward into the top of the closed shulker. Keep the camera and player position steady while the arrow travels, and hand off as soon as the arrow makes its first contact with the top of the shulker.
steps.exact_input: Release right mouse button
steps.success_cue: The arrow has been fired on a straight-down trajectory and has just reached the top surface of the closed shulker.

stor.handoff_condition: One ordinary arrow has just made first contact with the top of the stationary, closed NoAI shulker after being fired approximately straight downward by a Creative-mode player. Begin observation immediately without firing additional arrows, moving the shulker, or changing the player's aim.
uncertainties: The report provides no seed, coordinates, world type, or server requirement; a disposable single-player world and any clear, level test area are practical implementation choices.

The report does not specify the player's initial game mode before summoning the shulker. The plan executes /gamemode creative after summoning to preserve the report's listed order without treating the initial mode as a requirement.

The exact flight height and use of a fully drawn bow are not specified. Several blocks of height and a full draw are chosen to make the straight-down impact easy to execute; the report-supported critical condition is that the arrow strike the top of the closed shulker approximately vertically.

The report lists Creative players, closed shulkers, invulnerable mobs, and a breeze as affected targets, but its formal reproduction uses the supplied NoAI shulker command. This plan therefore covers only that deterministic variant.
No external verification was used because the report supplies the exact summon command and all version-sensitive conditions necessary for its stated reproduction path.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w10a in a single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled as a practical setup choice because the report requires a summon command but does not specify a game mode, seed, difficulty, multiplayer server, or other world settings.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version 20w10a rather than the fix version 24w37a or a later version.
Use a world in which the player can execute commands. A new Creative-mode world with commands enabled is the simplest setup.
Perform the test in an open area with enough horizontal space to see, approach, and aim at a summoned enderman without nearby blocks obstructing the shot.
Have one Crossbow, at least one Arrow, and at least one ordinary Firework Rocket available. The report does not specify custom firework NBT, colors, explosion stars, or flight duration.
Know the configured controls for Use Item/Place Block, Open Chat, and Open Inventory. With default controls these are right-click, T, and E, respectively.
Keep the offhand empty while loading the arrow control shot. Later, place the Firework Rocket in the offhand so the crossbow loads the rocket instead of another arrow.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using an installation configured for snapshot 20w10a. At the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 20w10a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running game version as 20w10a.

steps.action: Create or open a single-player Creative-mode test world with commands enabled. After joining, wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and movement and inventory input respond normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> set Game Mode to Creative and ensure commands/cheats are allowed -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a responsive Creative-mode world and can use commands.

steps.action: Move to an open, approximately level area. Open the Creative inventory, locate a Crossbow, an Arrow, and a Firework Rocket by their item names, and place them in accessible inventory or hotbar slots. Put the Crossbow in a known hotbar slot, keep the Arrow anywhere in the inventory, and keep the Firework Rocket out of the offhand for now.
steps.exact_input: Press E; use the Creative inventory or Search Items interface to obtain Crossbow, Arrow, and Firework Rocket; press E again to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Crossbow is available in the hotbar, an Arrow is in the inventory, a Firework Rocket is available for later use, and the offhand is empty.

steps.action: Select the Crossbow in the active hotbar slot. With the Arrow in the inventory and no Firework Rocket in the offhand, hold the Use Item control until the full crossbow-loading sequence and loading sound finish, then release the control.
steps.exact_input: Press the hotbar number assigned to the Crossbow; hold right-click until loading completes; release right-click.
steps.success_cue: The Crossbow remains in its visibly loaded state after right-click is released, with the arrow selected as its ammunition.

steps.action: While standing in the open test area, open in-game chat and execute the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash and the historical NBT syntax. Do not modernize or otherwise alter the command.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/summon enderman ~ ~ ~ {NoAI:1b}`, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A motionless enderman is present at or immediately beside the player's command-execution position.

steps.action: Allow the summoned entity and nearby terrain to finish rendering. Because the command summons the enderman at the player's current coordinates, move backward only as much as necessary to stop intersecting it and to see its body clearly.
steps.exact_input: Use S or another appropriate movement direction to move a short distance away, then release the movement control.
steps.success_cue: The enderman is clearly visible, remains stationary because of NoAI, and can be approached without a block obstructing the line of fire.

steps.action: Face the enderman and move forward until the player is at point-blank range—as close to the enderman's collision area as movement and entity pushing permit. Aim the crosshair at the central torso rather than above the head, below the feet, or beside the body.
steps.exact_input: Hold W while facing the enderman; release W when nearly touching it; adjust the mouse until the crosshair is centered on its torso.
steps.success_cue: The enderman fills much of the forward view, the player is at the closest stable position next to it, and the crosshair points into its torso.

steps.action: Fire the already-loaded arrow from the crossbow once while maintaining the point-blank position and torso aim. A loaded crossbow fires on a single Use Item press; do not begin another loading cycle before this shot.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The arrow control shot has made contact, indicated by the normal entity impact response such as an impact sound or brief damage animation, and the enderman remains available for the rocket test.

steps.action: Wait for the enderman's brief post-hit damage animation and damage-immunity interval to end before preparing the rocket shot. Do not repeatedly shoot it.
steps.exact_input: Wait approximately 1 second without attacking.
steps.success_cue: The enderman is no longer displaying the immediate damage flash from the arrow shot and is ready for a separate projectile attempt.

steps.action: Open the inventory and place the Firework Rocket in the shield-shaped offhand slot. Leave the Crossbow in its hotbar slot and leave the Arrow elsewhere in the inventory. Close the inventory after confirming the rocket is visibly held in the offhand.
steps.exact_input: Press E; drag the Firework Rocket to the offhand slot; press E to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Firework Rocket is held in the player's offhand, and the unloaded Crossbow remains accessible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Crossbow again. While the Firework Rocket is in the offhand, hold the Use Item control until the full loading sequence finishes, then release it. Keeping the rocket in the offhand during the complete loading sequence ensures that this crossbow shot is loaded with the rocket rather than the inventory arrow.
steps.exact_input: Press the Crossbow's hotbar number; hold right-click until loading completes; release right-click.
steps.success_cue: The Crossbow remains visibly loaded after the completed loading cycle, and the Firework Rocket was in the offhand throughout that cycle.

steps.action: If the arrow impact displaced the enderman or the player moved while managing the inventory, again approach until the player is at the closest stable point-blank position permitted by collision or entity pushing.
steps.exact_input: Face the enderman, hold W until nearly touching it, then release W.
steps.success_cue: The player has re-established point-blank range from the enderman.

steps.action: Steady the view so the crosshair points through the central portion of the enderman's torso. Confirm that the loaded Crossbow is still selected and avoid aiming at empty space between the enderman's legs or beyond the edges of its narrow body.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to center the crosshair on the enderman's torso; do not press right-click yet.
steps.success_cue: A loaded crossbow is selected, the player is at point-blank range, and the crosshair is centered on the enderman's torso.

steps.action: Fire the firework-loaded crossbow exactly once while maintaining the point-blank position and torso aim. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately as the shot is released; do not fire additional rockets or move away.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The loaded crossbow has just discharged its Firework Rocket toward the point-blank enderman, with no subsequent player action yet performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just fired one Firework Rocket from the loaded crossbow while standing at point-blank range and aiming at the stationary enderman's torso. Begin observation immediately, before the player moves, reloads, or fires another projectile.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, difficulty, or server type. A single-player Creative world with commands enabled is selected only to provide the required command access and items without adding combat, crafting, or exploration.

The report describes the required distance only as 'very close' and gives no numeric threshold. The plan operationalizes this as the closest stable point-blank position permitted by entity collision or pushing.

The report says only 'a fireworks rocket' and does not provide firework NBT, explosion-star contents, colors, or flight duration. The plan therefore uses an ordinary Firework Rocket obtained from the Creative inventory without custom data.

The offhand loading procedure is an operational method for ensuring that the crossbow loads the Firework Rocket while arrows remain in the inventory; the report itself does not specify hand placement or inventory arrangement.

The report uses the arrow shot as a control before the rocket shot. The short pause after the arrow impact is added to separate the two projectile attempts and avoid firing during the target's immediate post-hit interval.

source_meta._title: Player jitters when landing on a bed with the slow falling effect

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled as the minimal deterministic setup for obtaining a bed and executing the supplied effect command. Use default controls unless controls have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first version listed as affected.
Create or load a single-player world in Creative mode with cheats enabled.
Use a player as the falling entity; the report also mentions other entities, but its supplied reproduction specifically tests the player.
Locate a flat, solid area with enough unobstructed space to place both halves of a bed and to stand and jump on it.
Do not hold the Sneak control, which is Left Shift by default, while jumping, falling, landing, or waiting on the bed.
Keep the player on the bed after landing; do not walk off immediately.
Perform the landing before the supplied 100-second Slow Falling effect expires.

steps.action: Start or load a single-player Creative-mode world in Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 with cheats enabled. Wait for world loading to finish before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally, nearby terrain is rendered, Creative flight is available, and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Move to a flat area of solid ground. Choose a placement location where two adjacent floor blocks are available and the two blocks directly above them are unobstructed, because a bed occupies two horizontal block spaces.
steps.exact_input: Use the movement controls; defaults are W, A, S, and D.
steps.success_cue: A clear two-block-long bed placement area is visible and reachable.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory, obtain any color of bed, and put it into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory afterward.
steps.exact_input: Press E; select any bed from the Creative inventory; place it in a hotbar slot; press E or Esc to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A bed item is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the bed, aim at the top surface of the chosen ground block, and use the bed item to place it. If placement fails, move to a location with two adjacent floor blocks and clear space above them, then try again.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the bed's hotbar slot, then right-click the top of a ground block.
steps.success_cue: A complete bed, including both its foot and head halves, is placed on the ground.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and execute the report's Slow Falling command exactly as supplied. Include the leading slash because this command is being entered in player chat.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/effect give @s minecraft:slow_falling 100 0`, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without an error and the player receives the Slow Falling status effect.

steps.action: Confirm that Slow Falling is active before setting up the jump. In this version, an active status-effect icon should be visible on the HUD, and the effect can also be checked from the inventory screen.
steps.exact_input: If needed, press E to inspect active effects, then press E or Esc to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Slow Falling is still active and has enough remaining duration to complete one jump and landing.

steps.action: Walk onto the top surface of the placed bed and position the player near its center. Release all movement controls. Make sure the Sneak control is not pressed.
steps.exact_input: Use W, A, S, and D to move onto the bed; release those keys; do not press Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on top of the bed with Slow Falling active and is not sneaking.

steps.action: While remaining centered over the bed, jump vertically once. Do not hold a horizontal movement key, do not activate Creative flight by pressing Jump again, and do not press Sneak during the ascent or descent.
steps.exact_input: Press and release Space once; do not press Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: The player rises above the bed and begins descending toward the same bed under the Slow Falling effect.

steps.action: Allow the player to land on the bed without pressing movement, Jump, or Sneak. Keep the player on the bed and immediately hand control to the observation subsystem when bed contact occurs.
steps.exact_input: No input; in particular, do not press W, A, S, D, Space, or Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: The player's feet have contacted the bed while Slow Falling remains active, and the player has not walked or sneaked off the bed.

stor.handoff_condition: The Slow-Falling player has just landed on the top surface of the bed without sneaking and remains stationary on the bed. Begin observation immediately and continue through the post-landing bounce or settling period without supplying movement input.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, difficulty, or whether the test must use single-player or a dedicated server. Single-player Creative mode with cheats enabled is selected only as the simplest deterministic way to place a bed and run the supplied command.
The report does not specify a bed color or orientation; any bed is used because no color- or orientation-dependent condition is stated.
The instruction to 'Jump on top of the bed' is operationalized as a vertical jump from a stationary position centered on the bed so that the player deterministically lands on the same bed.
The report states that holding Shift prevents the issue, so the plan explicitly requires that Sneak not be held. This is a key negative input condition rather than an added reproduction requirement.
The supplied effect duration is preserved exactly. In-game setup after executing the command must be completed before the effect expires.

source_meta._title: Boats / rafts move into blocks when landing in less than one block deep water

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 16w04a in a fresh single-player Creative world. A Superflat world is recommended only to simplify construction. Use the normal Move Forward control, default W, and Change Perspective control, default F5. No dedicated server, multiplayer participant, seed, or absolute coordinates are required by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 16w04a, the first version listed in Affects versions. Do not use fix version 24w19a.
Use an unmodified client without mods that change boats, water, entity movement, or collision.
Ensure the Move Forward action is bound to a known key; the default is W.
Ensure the Use Item/Place Block action is bound to a known input; the default is right-click.
Prepare enough unobstructed space for a 13-by-13-block lower landing floor and a 3-by-16-block elevated water channel.
Use a normal wooden boat. Do not substitute a minecart or another vehicle. Bamboo rafts do not exist in the recommended historical version.

The exact screenshot-based structure is unavailable in the supplied report. The dimensions below are a deterministic practical reconstruction of the reported upper water level, waterfall, solid lower floor, and less-than-one-block-deep flowing water.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition snapshot 16w04a and start the game with that installation.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Java Edition 16w04a
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu and the displayed version is 16w04a.

steps.action: Create a fresh single-player Creative world. From the main menu, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, optionally select the Superflat world type under More World Options, and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat (recommended) -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player enters a new world in Creative mode and can fly and access unlimited inventory items.

steps.action: Wait before constructing anything until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding ground is visible, missing chunks are no longer present around the construction area, and movement responds without loading pauses.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and put a stack of solid building blocks, a Water Bucket, and one normal wooden Boat into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen. The Creative inventory Search Items tab can be used to find each item.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "stone", "water bucket", and "boat"
steps.success_cue: A solid block, a Water Bucket, and a normal wooden Boat are visible in the player's hotbar.

steps.action: Use the solid blocks to construct a flat 13-by-13-block lower landing floor. Keep the entire upper surface level, solid, and free of holes. This floor may be built directly on the Superflat ground.
steps.exact_input: Build a 13 x 13 solid horizontal floor
steps.success_cue: A level 13-by-13 solid floor with no gaps or blocks protruding above its surface is available for the lower flowing water.

steps.action: Choose one side of the lower floor as the launch side. Centered on that side, build the bottom of an elevated channel three blocks wide and sixteen blocks long. Set the channel floor three blocks above the lower landing floor. Extend its front end over the lower floor so a boat leaving the channel will fall toward the lower floor; extend the rest of the channel away from the lower floor to provide an acceleration runway.
steps.exact_input: Upper channel floor: 3 blocks wide x 16 blocks long; channel floor 3 blocks above lower landing floor
steps.success_cue: A straight three-block-wide runway is suspended above the lower floor, with its long axis pointing toward the lower landing area.

steps.action: Build a one-block-high wall along both long sides of the elevated channel and across its rear end. Leave the end facing the lower landing floor completely open so both water and the boat can pass over that edge.
steps.exact_input: Side walls: 16 blocks long and 1 block above the channel floor; rear wall: 3 blocks wide; front wall: none
steps.success_cue: The elevated structure is a straight water channel with two side walls, a closed rear, and an unobstructed open end above the lower floor.

steps.action: Select the Water Bucket and place water throughout the elevated channel until it contains a continuous, one-block-deep upper water surface suitable for boating. Place water directly in the channel cells rather than relying on one distant source to fill the runway. Allow water at the open end to spill downward onto the lower solid floor.
steps.exact_input: Select Water Bucket; right-click channel cells to place water
steps.success_cue: The upper channel has a continuous navigable water surface, and water is falling from its open end onto the lower floor.

steps.action: Wait until the water flow stops changing shape. Inspect the lower floor and verify that water from the fall spreads horizontally across the top of the solid floor. At least part of the intended landing path must contain visibly sloped or lower-than-full-block flowing water; do not replace the entire lower area with a flat pool of full source blocks.
steps.success_cue: A stable waterfall connects the upper channel to shallow flowing water lying directly on the lower solid floor.

steps.action: Remove any temporary support blocks, misplaced blocks, or other obstacles from the centerline between the rear of the upper channel, its open edge, and the shallow lower-water landing area. Do not remove the solid floor beneath the lower water.
steps.exact_input: Left-click unwanted obstruction blocks while in Creative mode
steps.success_cue: The boat has a straight, unobstructed route along the upper water, over the open edge, and into the lower flowing water.

steps.action: Move to the rear portion of the elevated channel. Select the Boat in the hotbar, aim at the upper water near the rear of the channel, and use the Boat on the water.
steps.exact_input: Select Boat; right-click the upper water near the closed rear end
steps.success_cue: One normal boat is floating in the upper channel with most of the sixteen-block runway between it and the open end.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that using the boat does not place water or blocks. Aim at the boat and use it to enter the boat.
steps.exact_input: Select empty hotbar slot; right-click the boat
steps.success_cue: The player's viewpoint is attached to the boat and the player can control it.

steps.action: Before beginning the run, steer the boat into the center of the channel and face it directly toward the open end and lower landing area. Use brief taps of Move Left and Move Right, default A and D, as needed. Do not begin the full-speed run until the boat is aligned and still has most of the runway ahead.
steps.exact_input: A and D as brief steering taps
steps.success_cue: The occupied boat is near the rear of the upper channel, centered between the side walls, and pointed straight toward the open end.

steps.action: Switch to the rear third-person camera recommended in the report comment so the channel edge and landing path remain visible. Press Change Perspective repeatedly only until the camera is behind the player and boat.
steps.exact_input: F5, repeated until rear third-person view is active
steps.success_cue: The boat, the runway ahead, and the open end of the channel are visible from behind the player.

steps.action: Press and continuously hold Move Forward, default W. Keep holding it as the boat accelerates down the upper water channel. Use only small steering corrections if needed, and do not brake, dismount, or release Move Forward before reaching the edge.
steps.exact_input: Hold W; optionally tap A or D briefly without releasing W
steps.success_cue: The occupied boat is traveling quickly and straight toward the open end after using the available upper-water runway to accelerate.

steps.action: Continue holding Move Forward while allowing the boat to pass completely over the open end of the upper channel, fall toward the lower floor, and make its first contact with the shallow flowing water above that floor. Do not dismount or release Move Forward before contact, and do not repeat the landing before handing off to observation.
steps.exact_input: Continue holding W through departure, fall, and first water contact
steps.success_cue: The occupied boat has just contacted the lower shallow flowing water above the solid floor while Move Forward remains held.

stor.handoff_condition: The occupied boat has just made its first contact with the shallow flowing water above the lower solid floor while the Move Forward input remains held. Begin observation immediately, before releasing the input, dismounting, moving the boat again, or repeating the run.
uncertainties: The report relies on a screenshot whose contents and exact dimensions are not included in the supplied text. The 13-by-13 lower floor, 3-by-16 upper channel, and three-block elevation are practical reconstruction choices rather than dimensions asserted by the report.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, construction material, exact drop height, or required game mode. A fresh Creative Superflat world and solid stone-like blocks are selected solely to make the setup deterministic and quick to construct.

The lower landing water must remain flowing and less than one full block deep, as stated by the title and description. Turning the lower area into a full source-water pool would remove a stated trigger condition.
The original report says only to grab a boat and recommends reproducing at full speed while holding W. Any normal wooden boat available in 16w04a is therefore acceptable.

Web verification was limited to checking the version-sensitive control behavior: available Minecraft Wiki history confirms that 16w04a boats use the normal forward/backward and left/right movement actions, consistent with the report's W instruction. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E8%88%B9?utm_source=openai))
A comment mentions 1.20.4, but that version is not present in the report's Affects versions field and is therefore not added to affected_versions.
Bamboo rafts are included in the report title because later affected versions support them, but the recommended first affected version, Minecraft 16w04a, must be tested with a boat.
